description: This updated edition of the best-selling Small Engines and Power Equipment is more than a simple engine repair manual. Designed for the beginner with little or no mechanical experience, this book is a graphically appealing, step-by-step guide that covers all of the most important engine maintenance and repair skills you'll need to keep your equipment running at peak performance. It also shows exactly how to perform mechanical upkeep and repairs on the most common outdoor power implements. With new and improved content for today's motorized equipment, this DIY bible includes engine and mechanical repair plus maintenance instruction for all your outdoor power equipment , including lawn mowers, snow blowers, chain saws, power washers, generators, leaf blowers, rototillers, wood splitters, lawn edgers, and weed whips. With clear how-to photos and detailed diagrams , you'll see exactly what needs to be done. A comprehensive troubleshooting guide helps you define problems and enact solutions. Among the many skills you'll learn are seasonal tune-ups, changing oil, servicing spark plugs, cleaning filters, replacing muffler, servicing the fuel tank, overhauling the carburetor, servicing brakes, inspecting flywheels, replacing the fuel pump, and replacing a rewind cord. With Small Engines and Outdoor Power Equipment 2nd Edition in your library, you won't need to haul the lawn mower off to the repair center and wait a few weeks just because a filter is plugged or the old gas needs to be replaced. description: Before you buy another part, find out why your engine won’t run. The mower starts, sputters, and quits. The chainsaw worked last season but refuses to cooperate today. Your generator sits ready for an emergency—until you try to start it. You pull again. Change the plug. Search for a video. Someone says it’s the carburetor. Someone else says it’s the ignition coil. Soon, you have several possible answers—and no clear idea which one fits your machine. What should you check first? What does the result mean? And what should you do next? Those are the questions a useful repair handbook needs to answer. You do not need to become a mechanic overnight. You need a practical way to understand what you are looking at, check the likely causes, and make your next decision with something better than a hunch. The Only Small Engine Repair Handbook for Beginners by Austin K. Starr helps you build that approach. Using the See It, Do It, Check It method, this illustrated guide connects component identification with practical checks and clear next steps. Start with accessible inspections, understand what your findings suggest, and learn when further testing—or professional help—is needed. Inside, you’ll learn how to: Give a no-start problem a sensible starting point. Work through fuel, air, spark, and compression checks instead of treating every symptom as a reason to buy a carburetor. Approach carburetor work with less uncertainty. Understand the parts, document linkages, and follow cleaning and reassembly guidance without relying on memory. Recognize the differences that matter between two-stroke and four-stroke engines. description: It ran last year. Why won't it start now? Your lawn mower won't start, the chainsaw dies after a few seconds, or the generator you need tonight just coughs. Before you pay for a repair or buy a new machine, open this manual. Most small engine problems come down to a few simple causes, and you can find and fix them yourself with basic tools, a little patience and the right safety habits. Written for homeowners with no mechanical background, Small Engine Repair Manual for Beginners walks you through each job in plain English, with numbered steps, clear illustrations and a safety box wherever there is a hazard. Where a setting varies from one machine to another, the book gives you the typical figure and shows you where to find the exact one for yours, so you never work from a guess. Inside you'll find: ■ A 15-minute diagnosis that checks fuel, spark, air and compression in the right order ■ Troubleshooting flowcharts for engines that won't start, start and die, surge, run rough, smoke or vibrate ■ Fuel and ethanol problems, carburetor cleaning and adjustment, spark plugs, air filters and oil changes ■ Recoil and electric starter repairs, plus a clear look at compression and valves ■ Machine-by-machine care for push and riding mowers, chainsaws, string trimmers and leaf blowers, generators and snowblowers ■ A season-by-season maintenance calendar, spec tables, service logs and a symptom index ■ A straightforward guide to when a repair is worth it, and when to call a pro or replace the machine You'll also learn how to build a beginner tool kit for under $100, and how to read your machine's model numbers so you buy the right part the first time. description: How a Small Engine Works A Clear Guide to Understanding Small Engines and Why They Fail Small engines power the equipment people rely on every day. Lawn mowers, snowblowers, generators, pressure washers, pumps, and utility machines all depend on compact engines designed to deliver reliable power with very few parts. Yet when these engines run poorly or fail, the cause often feels confusing and unpredictable. This book explains what is actually happening inside a small engine, using clear language and real-world examples. It focuses on how fuel, air, ignition, compression, lubrication, cooling, and load interact in simple mechanical systems and why small engines react so quickly when something is wrong. This book teaches understanding. It shows how to read engine behavior, recognize symptoms, and trace problems back to the system involved. Surging, stalling under load, hard starting, overheating, backfiring, and sudden failures are explained logically instead of treated as mysteries. Inside this book you will learn: • How small engines convert fuel into usable motion • Why small engines stall instead of powering through resistance • The real differences between two-stroke and four-stroke engines • How carburetors, governors, and ignition systems actually work • Why air cooling and cleanliness matter so much • How load, shaft orientation, and equipment design affect behavior • How to diagnose problems by symptom rather than guessing • What mistakes commonly shorten engine life This book is written for equipment owners, DIY-minded readers, and anyone who wants a solid understanding of how small engines work. description: Your mower won't start. Your generator keeps dying. You don't know if it's fuel, spark, or something worse — and you're tired of guessing. Most repair books force you to learn engine anatomy before you can find your answer. They're organized by system — fuel, ignition, compression — when what you actually have is a symptom . This book fixes that. Small Engine Diagnosis is organized the way you actually experience problems: by what's happening, not by what's inside. Won't start. Starts then dies. Runs rough. Smokes. Leaks. Loses power. Flip to your symptom, follow the decision tree, and get a specific answer — not a shrug and a list of five equally likely guesses. What makes this different: The Engine Profile Filter — a one-time, 10-minute setup that narrows every diagnosis to your specific engine (2-stroke or 4-stroke, carbureted or fuel-injected, and more), instead of generic advice that half-applies to your machine Symptom-first navigation — no need to understand engine systems before you start; just find what you're seeing and go Every decision tree ends somewhere specific — a real fix, or a clear "this needs a professional" — never an unhelpful list of maybes Color-coded smoke diagnosis, leak-location trees, and a Repair-or-Replace framework so you stop wasting money on the wrong parts Covers: mowers, generators, snowblowers, trimmers, pressure washers, and chainsaws. Whether you're a homeowner trying to avoid another repair shop bill, an off-grid or rural reader who needs equipment working now , or someone flipping used small engines and needs to diagnose before you buy — this book gets you from symptom to solution fast. title: The Illustrated Small Engine Repair Handbook: Step-by-Step Troubleshooting, Repair & Maint
description: Find the next useful test and follow a clear repair process without scattered instructions or parts guesswork. Does your engine crank without starting, run briefly and stop, or lose power when the work begins? Have you cleaned or replaced a part and still been left with the same symptom? Do you want illustrated steps that help you inspect, test, service, and check your equipment with a clear purpose? Different faults can produce similar symptoms. A wet spark plug, an unstable idle, or a low compression reading needs a method and context before it can support a repair decision. Disconnected tips rarely show how those observations fit together. Start with what the machine does, then follow the evidence through the job. The Illustrated Small Engine Repair Handbook combines symptom charts, representative component illustrations, numbered workshop procedures, and checks after the repair. It covers common single-cylinder gasoline engines used in lawn mowers, generators, chainsaws, trimmers, snowblowers, and other outdoor power equipment. Build a repair process you can use at the workbench. Symptom-based troubleshooting : follow routes for no rotation, no start, starting and stopping, surging, smoke, hot failure, vibration, and failed stopping controls. Illustrated fuel and carburetor service : distinguish metal float-bowl, plastic modular, and diaphragm designs, record hoses and linkage, and check sealing before returning to use. Ignition and starting procedures : work through spark testing, stop circuits, spark plugs, flywheel inspection, recoil starting, and low-voltage electric-start checks. Measurements with context : understand units, valve-clearance measurement, compression-test limitations, and the importance of exact model specifications. Equipment and seasonal checks

description: Diagnose and Fix Lawn Mowers, Snowblowers, Generators, Chainsaws and More Small engines power the equipment people rely on every day. When they fail, the problem often feels complicated, expensive, and frustrating. The truth is most small engine problems come from a handful of common causes. Once you understand how these engines actually work, diagnosing them becomes straightforward. This guide walks you through the real mechanics behind small engine failures and shows you how to track down problems quickly and safely. Whether you are working on a lawn mower that will not start, a snowblower that keeps stalling, or a generator that lost power, this book breaks the process down into clear steps that anyone can follow. Inside this book you will learn how to: • Identify the four things every engine needs to run • Diagnose fuel system problems and bad gasoline • Troubleshoot carburetors without guessing • Test ignition systems and spark problems • Understand compression issues and internal wear • Fix common starting failures • Track down surging, power loss, and stalling • Recognize warning signs before serious damage happens • Perform simple maintenance that prevents most failures The book also explains the systems inside the machines many homeowners use every season, including: • Lawn mowers • Snowblowers • Chainsaws • Generators • Pressure washers • Other small engine equipment Instead of complicated theory, the focus is on practical understanding. You will see how air, fuel, compression, and spark interact, how carburetors meter fuel, and how common failures develop over time.
